They say firelight only illuminates three inches, yet I feel it can pierce through a hundred fathoms of loess. Lately, I keep hearing the sound of water being chiseled from the well’s depths—tell me, is it an echo from a century ago, or a harbinger of a century to come?
Keep this lamp with you. When the wellwater rises past the gravel someday, remember to scoop a ladle and pour it into the lamp.

5397890951957101625:
A Mohist came from the north, claiming to have a strategy to save the world. Yanguang heard of this and eagerly invited him into his residence.

At first, the Mohist entered the residence with an air of arrogance, repeatedly presenting his strategies to Yanguang. When they were not accepted, he prepared to leave. Yanguang then made a promise to the Mohist: if he could recreate the legendary automaton of the ancient craftsman Deheng, which could operate continuously for ten days without stopping, his advice would be heeded. The Mohist agreed and completed the task in just over a month. On the ninth day of operation, the automaton showed no signs of stopping. On the tenth day, the Mohist requested funds to prepare for the construction of a canal along the Yellow River. Yanguang laughed heartily and led the Mohist to inspect the automaton—only to find its mechanisms misaligned and broken. Suspicious, the Mohist examined it and discovered a wooden peg that did not fit the design. Yanguang then made another promise: if the Mohist could drink a hundred jars of wine in his residence, his strategies would be accepted.

How foolish and laughable! Who knows if that Mohist ever drank all hundred jars?

Did Yanguang truly wish to save the world? Or did he merely seek to impress the emperor and regain favor?
Did the emperor truly wish to save the world? By submitting to the Khitans, avoiding conflict, and chasing fame in the annals of history?
Did the Mohist truly wish to save the world? To think that clever tricks and crafts could save the world—such a notion was unheard of!

Now we see them all as clowns leaping for fame and profit, merely playing tricks on us common folk. National policies? People's policies? World-saving strategies? What good do they do for you? What good do they do for me? Like delirious ramblings, they become mere jokes.
